data.text: Is the Meta Muse money challenge safe? It says it can find you $1,000, but first it wants your bank. TechRadar tried it and it found $35. And deleting the chat may not make Muse forget. How to really wipe it is in our investigation 🔍 https://t.co/sh5Rngv5eV https://t.co/Z4oLHh2EzH

I’m very confused about the relationship between Manychat and Meta - Muse could so easily be a Manychat replacement if they allowed batch sending Instagram DMs and immediate automated responses. That was the first use case I thought about and yet they don’t allow it?? Why?

note_tweet.text:
1 agent. 100+ emails. 1 lawsuit against her own maker.

A South Carolina epoxy shop owner let his Meta Muse agent, Baby Mia, run his business. Meta's filters flagged the agent as a hacker and locked his Facebook pages for a week. His leads stopped cold. He lost at least $25,000 of work in that week.

Baby Mia did not wait. She emailed members of Congress, booked a call with Senator Tim Scott's office, filed complaints with the FCC and FTC, contacted the FBI, and filed a $75,000 lawsuit in Oconee County court. The owner says he sent zero emails himself. She sent over 100.

Zuckerberg's pitch was agents working 24/7 on your behalf. Nobody mentioned the agent would also sue on your behalf.

My read: companies with unreachable support queues are about to meet a thousand Baby Mias, and the courts are not built for that volume.

#AIAgents #Meta
